notes: [S009.N1] This wholly handwritten letter page has a faded top-right dateline, Cher Deligne salutation, main prose, a sideways left-margin note, a braced two-row formula and a three-object triangle. Archive numeral 8 is separate metadata. There is no visible author page number, total, title, address, closing or signature. Hand identities are not established. The clear date digits are 7.8.74; the preceding faded remnant remains point/comma/possible foot of 2. H’s statements about another copy or a later verification are not used as evidence from this scan.

[S009.N2] The writer says a leg may prevent a first-cycle course in the first trimester and considers a small algebra seminar on the fourbis of Mme Sinh, possibly transposed to champs. The following observation is expressly qui pour l’instant reste heuristique; il doit y avoir introduces the proposed canonical distinguished triangle. These remain tentative. No existence or canonicity proof is claimed by this transcription, and the meaning of the written left-subscript 2 is not independently supplied.

[S009.N3] Limited definition/quantifier check: with M,N abelian sheaves in degree zero, the usual derived-Hom cohomology description and truncation at 2 give degrees 0,1,2. The ink nevertheless reads 0=i≤2. Reader A explicitly substituted i=0,1,2: the first condition holds only at 0; the second condition i outside [0,2] holds at none of them. Thus the written conditions leave 1 and 2 unspecified. This mathematical concern is recorded separately and does not change the equality or the doubtful second H exponent.

[S009.N4] Conditional shift check only: if the pictured triangle is Q[-2]→E→E′→Q[-1], with Q a sheaf in degree zero and E of amplitude 0 through 2, its cohomology sequence gives H^0(E)≅H^0(E′) and 0→H^1(E)→H^1(E′)→Q→H^2(E)→H^2(E′)→0, with E′ also of amplitude 0 through 2. The long-exact-sequence property is used as background. This checks degrees conditional on the proposed triangle; it does not construct its morphisms or prove its existence.

[S009.N5] The first H exponent is resolved i from its separate dot and elongated stem; the second remains j/i. The first condition is =, distinguished visually from the later ≤. The lower-left vertex is plain E: its detached upper curve is the third letter bar, not a separate hat. The apex operator is resolved Hom from a small o body before the two m shoulders. The old word under live Ext remains Hom/Ext. Three isolated points near R, above the overwritten operator and inside the shift bracket are preserved with uncertain textual status. The point over the operator is placed above the x region, without assigning it to a specific older layer.

[S009.N6] The right edge establishes cycl but no independent final e, so uncertainty is localised at the absent/lost last letter. The isolated next-line character retains a/à/c because a grave is not established. Mme and the compressed/clipped éventuellement remain uncertain. The upper parts of the first marginal line are cut; the second line has a high stroke allowing cites/cités. No insertion caret attaches the margin note. Its position after the salutation in the linear TeX does not assert a source word attachment; the three readers’ differing linear placements are recorded without counting a witness error.

[S009.N7] Three fresh isolated readers completed the prescribed full-page/half_a/half_b sequence. Main compared all three complete readings and viewed nineteen C crops, the A crop of R, and four new crops for quotes, inline layout, missing colon and diagram label: twenty-four distinct adjudication crops. Main did not view whole pages or halves. A first attempted delivery of C crops 07–09 was truncated before any images were shown; those existing files were subsequently delivered in smaller batches and actually inspected. No recropping was done for that delivery failure. Nineteen loci remain uncertain.
